title: Direct mass measurements of the high-spin isomers in self-conjugate 94Ag
byline: Virtanen; Ville; Reponen; Mikael; Dao; Duy Duc; Nowacki; Frédéric; Eronen; Tommi; Kankainen; Anu; Beliuskina; Olga; Caceres; Lucia; Chinthakayala; Saikumar; De
html:
Abstract:Two decades ago, two-proton emission from a $(21^+)$ isomeric state in $^{94}$Ag was reported. This report has remained the sole example of possible two-proton radioactivity in a nucleus with an odd number of protons on the chart of nuclei. A debate regarding the viability of the decay mode has been ongoing due to the unknown mass of the isomer. Here, using state-selective laser ionization in a hot cavity catcher, we present multi-reflection time-of-flight mass spectrometry of the long-lived isomeric states of $^{94}$Ag and its one-proton decay daughter $^{93}$Pd. For the first time, direct mass measurements of the $(7^+)$ and $(21^+)$ isomeric states set the stage for an independent discussion of the energetics of these decays. We rule out the two-proton emission from the $(21^+)$ state as previously reported and reveal the one-proton decay energy to be significantly lower. State-of-the-art shell-model calculations reproduce the energy gap of the $(7^+)$ and the $(21^+)$ states as well as the half-life of the $(21^+)$ state, implying the $(21^+)$ state is likely near-spherical, contradicting the reported explanation for the two-proton radioactivity. Importantly, the techniques employed are a stepping stone towards the first laser spectroscopic investigation of a proton-emitting state
